title: The Con Artist Who Sold The Eiffel Tower Twice
sources: Smithsonian Magazine (2012), 'The Man Who Sold the Eiffel Tower. Twice.'
History.com (2018), 'How a Con Artist Sold the Eiffel Tower'
The New York Times (1947), obituary of 'Count' Victor Lustig

lines.text: In 1925, a smooth-talking con artist named Victor Lustig
lines.caps: In 1925, | a smooth-talking | con artist named | Victor Lustig

lines.text: sold the Eiffel Tower for scrap metal.
And then, a month later... he sold it again.
See, Paris was struggling with the tower's massive repair bills,
so Victor forged fake government seals
and invited the city's top scrap dealers to a luxury hotel.
He whispered that the city was secretly tearing the tower down,
and accepted a massive suitcase of cash from a gullible dealer.
Victor hopped the first train to Austria with fifty thousand dollars.
The victim was so utterly humiliated
that he never even called the police.
So six months later, Victor returned to Paris,
found another dealer, and tried to sell it a second time!
